issues.title: [Bug] v4.6.7 startup unconditionally VACUUMs multi-GB logs, saturating disk; retention compares seconds to milliseconds
issues.root_cause: `cleanup_old_logs` in `proxy_db.rs` calculated cutoff using `timestamp()` (seconds) while `ProxyRequestLog` stored millisecond timestamps. Furthermore, it ran `VACUUM` unconditionally on every app boot even when 0 records were deleted, freezing disk I/O for minutes on multi-gigabyte log databases.
issues.how_fixed: Calculated cutoff using `timestamp_millis()` for millisecond alignment and conditioned `VACUUM` execution strictly to runs where `deleted > 0`.

### 🛠️ 修复原理
1. **毫秒时间戳对齐**：将 `cleanup_old_logs` 的过滤基准统一为 `chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis()`，防止因秒/毫秒单位不匹配导致日志未按预期清理。

issues.title: Token acquisition timeout 5s under high concurrency / deadlock
issues.root_cause: The token manager imposed a rigid 5-second hard timeout on `get_token`. Under high multi-agent concurrency (e.g. Cursor and Claude Code sending requests simultaneously), synchronous file locks, un-cached config JSON reads (`load_app_config`), and in-band OAuth refresh calls serialized workers and triggered false timeouts.
issues.how_fixed: Expanded token acquisition timeout to 15s (`Duration::from_secs(15)`). Replaced blocking file I/O on the hot path with `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. Implemented double-checked locking for account token refreshes, an in-memory TTL cache for configuration, and detached pending account reloads to background tasks.
issues.github_markdown_reply:

- **Eliminated Hot-Path Disk Lock Contention**: All disk persistence (`accounts.json` update) has been offloaded to background blocking tasks with non-blocking memory caches.
- **Double-Checked Locking**: Prevented duplicate OAuth refresh stampedes when multiple agent threads wake up at once.

issues.title: Account bans, 403 Forbidden, and Google ToS violations
issues.root_cause: Upstream injected a static physical machine GUID and shared session ID across all rotated accounts. Google's anti-abuse heuristics easily correlated multiple accounts to a single machine fingerprint. Additionally, any upstream 403 unconditionally wrote `is_forbidden = true` to disk, permanently deleting accounts even on transient rate limits or Google verification challenges.
issues.how_fixed: Implemented per-account virtual hardware isolation in `src-tauri/src/modules/device.rs`, generating isolated deterministic UUIDs and headers (`mac_machine_id`, `session_id`). Designed a 3-tier `ForbiddenKind` classification in `token_manager.rs` and handlers: `VALIDATION_REQUIRED` triggers a 10-minute cooldown, transient 403s enter a 5-minute memory quarantine, and permanent policy bans require verifiable evidence before updating disk.
issues.github_markdown_reply:
Hello! Account ban triggers and the 403 deletion cascade have been completely resolved in **[Antigravity-Shield](https://github.com/DoctorGuidance/Antigravity-Shield)**:

### 🛡️ Anti-Detection & Safe Quarantine Architecture
1. **Isolated Device Fingerprinting**: Each account has its own isolated virtual device profile and machine ID, preventing Google from linking multiple accounts to a single hardware hash.
2. **3-Tier 403 Quarantine**: Temporary 403 errors and verification challenges are quarantined in memory for 5–10 minutes instead of being destructively marked as banned on disk.
